commit.subject: docs(ledger): session matching on request, redaction, hook and worktree rules

entries.text:
A reviewer (GPT-6.1-Sol) checked your 6 commits at 4e695f9 and verified the findings below. The checkout is now on branch fix/codex-review (4 display fixes by another agent on top of yours). Create branch fix/ledger-review from it and fix all six there at the root cause, each with a test that reproduces the reviewer's input first (see it fail, then fix).

Coordinator decisions:
- P1 secret in title: redact every free-text field of the entry (thread title, labels, commit subject is fine as is), and add a test that scans the whole encoded ledger JSON for the planted secret.
- P1 session fallback: off by default. Enable it only with an explicit flag (e.g. `--match-sessions`), only for sessions from the given --codex-home/source that made file edits (an edit/write/patch action, or a shell command that writes), and if more than one session qualifies, attach none and report the commit as ambiguous instead of guessing. Explicit `--session <id>` (repeatable) attributes those sessions directly. Update the CI docs and the example in docs/production.md accordingly (CI uses a job-local CODEX_HOME, so --match-sessions is safe there).
- P2s: as the reviewer suggests. For the hook: read all pushed refs first; skip the nested ledger push when the outer push includes agent-ledger; never block or fail the user's push because of ledger trouble (warn instead); only overwrite/remove a hook whose content is byte-identical to what we generated.

Servers: use PORT=4782 if you need one; 4777, 4779 are other people's, never touch them. Same verification and commit rules as before. Report commits and verification.

Review findings:

── assistant · just now
I found six defects. All references are at `4e695f9`. I verified them by code inspection through git. I did not run tests or change the checkout.

- **P1: A secret in the first prompt line is published as the thread title.** `src/server/CodexRollouts.ts:120`, `src/server/Ledger.ts:517`.
  - Input: a prompt starting with `Use API_TOKEN=[redacted] to fix this`, followed by an action that matches a commit. The message is redacted, but `thread.title` keeps the secret. `--no-outputs` does not remove it.
  - What I'd do here is redact thread metadata and label values before encoding the complete ledger entry. Add a test that checks the entire JSON for the secret.

  ```text
  Prompt → raw thread title → ledger JSON → origin
  ```

- **P1: The session fallback can attach someone else's work to a commit.** `src/core/ledger.ts:134`, `src/server/Ledger.ts:490`.
  - Input: the parent commit is at 09:00. The editing session ends at 10:00. A read-only review session runs `git diff` and ends at 10:04. CI commits the edits at 10:05. The review session wins because it ended last. Sessions in other worktrees also qualify.
  - The fix is to require an explicit session ID for CI attribution. Keep this fallback disabled by default. Add a test with an editor and a later read-only reviewer.

  ```text
  Editor ends → reviewer ends → CI commits
                      └────────→ reviewer selected
  ```

- **P2: Updating the ledger ref can move a checked-out worktree's HEAD.** `src/server/Ledger.ts:430`.
  - Input: another worktree has `agent-ledger` checked out at L0, while origin has L1. Run `sync --push` from the code worktree with no new entries. The service updates the shared ledger ref to L1. The other worktree's HEAD moves, but its index and files stay at L0.
  - What I'd do here is check every worktree before updating the ref, and refuse to move a checked-out ledger branch. The tests only check HEAD while the code branch is checked out.

  ```text
  update-ref agent-ledger → other worktree HEAD moves
                         → index and files stay unchanged
  ```

- **P2: The hook can make a valid atomic push fail.** `src/core/ledger.ts:215`, `src/core/ledger.ts:222`.
  - Input: origin's ledger is L0, the local ledger is L1, and code has a new commit. Run `git push --atomic origin main agent-ledger`. The hook's nested push advances origin's ledger to L2. The outer push still requests L0 → L1, so Git rejects it. With `--atomic`, the code push fails too.
  - The fix is to read all hook input before doing any sync. If the outer push includes `agent-ledger`, do not push that ref from inside the hook. Add a real combined atomic-push test. The current hook test uses a fake CLI that never moves refs.

  ```text
  Outer push plans L0 → L1
    Hook pushes L0 → L2
  Outer push uses stale L0 → rejected
  ```

- **P2: A marker comment is enough to overwrite or delete a user-modified hook.** `src/server/Ledger.ts:589`, `src/server/Ledger.ts:610`.
  - Input: install the hook, then add a user push check before its final `exit 0`. A second install removes that check. Uninstall deletes the whole file. Both operations accept the marker anywhere in the file as proof of ownership.
  - What I'd do here is refuse replacement or removal when the generated script has been modified. Add tests for a marked hook with user additions. The current refusal test only covers an unmarked file.

- **P2: Ledger sync ignores a Codex home containing only archived sessions.** `src/server/Ledger.ts:279`, `src/server/Ledger.ts:305`.
  - Input: `CODEX_HOME` contains `archived_sessions/rollout-…jsonl`, but no `sessions/` directory. `--source codex-rollouts` fails. `auto` silently skips the source, although `CodexRollouts` supports both directories.
  - The fix is straightforward: check both directories, or let the reader return an empty listing. Add an archived-only fixture test.
The commit-6 state matches my final files byte for byte. Committing it, then the docs.

entries.title: git commit -q -F - <<EOF 2>&1 · for f in AGENTS.md README.md · do cmp -s $f <path>/$f · done · read docs/spec.md, <path>/spec.md · read docs/production.md, <path>/production.md · git add AGENTS.md README.md docs · git commit -q -F - <<EOF2 2>&1 · git log --oneline -9 · git status --short · docs(ledger): session matching on request, redaction, hook and worktree rules · The CI example uses a job-local CODEX_HOME with --match-sessions · --session · names a session when the job knows it. · Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com> · EOF2
entries.command:
cd . && git -c user.email=<private> commit -q -F - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v "^\[" ; sleep 2; for f in AGENTS.md README.md; do cmp -s $f <path>/$f && echo "ok $f"; done; cmp -s docs/spec.md <path>/spec.md && cmp -s docs/production.md <path>/production.md && echo "ok docs"; git add AGENTS.md README.md docs && git -c user.email=<private> commit -q -F - <<'EOF2' 2>&1 | grep -v "^\["; git log --oneline -9; git status --short
fix(ledger): read a Codex home that holds only archived sessions

The ledger checked for `sessions/` alone, so a Codex home with only
`archived_sessions/` failed `--source codex-rollouts` and was skipped by
auto, though the rollout reader lists both. Both now use one list of
rollout folders.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
docs(ledger): session matching on request, redaction, hook and worktree rules

The CI example uses a job-local CODEX_HOME with --match-sessions; --session
names a session when the job knows it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF2
